llm.summary: The skill's instructions mostly match its stated purpose (convert PDFs to bilingual markdown), but there are inconsistencies and unexplained file-system/venv assumptions that could lead to unintended file reads/writes or indexing of sensitive content.

dimensions.detail: The name and description match the actions described in SKILL.md: extracting text from PDFs and producing Italian and English markdown files. The declared dependencies (pdftotext, python3, a venv) are reasonable for PDF extraction and processing. However, the skill assumes a specific local repository layout under ~/Documenti/github/polito/ and references a virtual environment variable ($VENV) without declaring it — this is an implicit assumption about the user's environment that should have been made explicit.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions direct the agent to read the user's home directory (~/Documenti/github/polito/), list and open existing course folders, and integrate new content into existing notes (update vs create). Those file reads/writes are coherent with the stated purpose but carry the risk of overwriting or reading unrelated local files. The SKILL.md also mandates 'Zero information loss' (include every formula/example/caveat) which could cause inclusion of sensitive data present in PDFs. The instructions reference $VENV and a path (~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/lookupmark-local-rag/...) for querying the local-rag tool; $VENV is not declared in requires.env, and the two venv paths mentioned in the file are inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest install risk. It relies on system binaries (pdftotext, python3) being present; that is reasonable and expected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials but repeatedly references a $VENV variable and specific local paths (two different venv paths are mentioned). This mismatch (using $VENV while declaring no env vars) is an incoherence: the agent may fail or pick a wrong venv, and the skill implicitly assumes access to particular local runtime environments. No external credentials are requested, which is appropriate, but the undeclared env var and hard-coded home-directory paths are concerning.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills. It writes outputs into the user's repository and requests the automatic local-rag indexing to pick up produced files — this will make newly created notes discoverable by the local RAG system (daily cron and optional immediate querying). That behavior is expected for its purpose but the user should be aware that generated content becomes part of local search/indexing and could expose included PDF content to other tools.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill: 1) Confirm you want an agent that will read and write under ~/Documenti/github/polito/ (it will check existing folders and may update or overwrite notes). Back up that directory if you care about current files. 2) Ask the skill author to clarify the virtual environment usage: SKILL.md references $VENV and two different venv paths but declares no env var — ensure which venv should be used or set $VENV yourself. 3) Understand 'Zero information loss' means everything in the PDF may be reproduced verbatim into markdown; don’t run this on PDFs containing private or sensitive data you do not want indexed. 4) If you rely on local-rag, note the files will be indexed automatically (daily cron) and are searchable by other local tools; if that is undesired, disable indexing or move outputs to a private folder. 5) If you want higher confidence, request from the maintainer: (a) explicit list of declared env vars (including VENV), (b) a safe-update policy (e.g., create backups or write to a new folder rather than merging by default), and (c) an explicit confirmation of where files are written and how conflicts are handled.
